title: Bharatlabs
overview: A diagnostics and healthcare services platform delivered across web and Android, with a compliant enterprise payment solution at its core. Listed in the delivered-projects portfolio as a healthcare SaaS build with both a live site and a Play Store application.
problem: Diagnostic bookings and patient payments were fragmented across offline collection, manual reconciliation and non-compliant payment handling — blocking scale and creating regulatory exposure.
businessContext: Healthcare payments carry HIPAA obligations alongside Indian payment-gateway constraints. The platform had to serve both a consumer app audience and lab-side operations without splitting the data model.
discovery: Mapped the current-state booking-to-report journey across web, app and offline touchpoints to locate the drop-offs between test selection, payment and report delivery.
research: Journey interviews with patients and lab staff, plus reconciliation-log analysis to quantify failed and manually-settled transactions.
prd: Unified catalogue of tests, packages and pricing across web and app
Compliant payment capture with retry, refund and reconciliation states
Booking lifecycle: slot → collection → processing → report
Role-based operations console for lab staff
Consent and data-handling flows aligned to HIPAA expectations
architecture: Shared API layer serving the responsive web app and the Android client
Payment gateway integration with idempotent transaction handling
Report storage with access-scoped delivery to the booking owner
Audit logging on every record touch for compliance review
wireframes: Low-fidelity flows were produced for booking, checkout and report retrieval before build, then validated with lab operations before UI polish.
challenges: Keeping payment retries idempotent across flaky mobile networks
Aligning compliance requirements with a fast consumer checkout
Parity between web and Android release cycles
tradeoffs: Shipped web-first with the Android client following, rather than delaying both for simultaneous launch
Chose a single unified catalogue over per-partner catalogues to reduce operational overhead at launch
outcome: Delivered a HIPAA-compliant enterprise payment solution that improved patient transactions by 22%, shipped live on the web and the Google Play Store.
learnings: In regulated healthcare, the compliance model has to be designed into the checkout, not layered on after
Operations staff are the real power users — their console determines whether the consumer funnel works
roadmap: Report intelligence and longitudinal patient history
businessValue: Turned an offline, manually-reconciled diagnostics workflow into a compliant digital revenue channel.

title: Finixpe
tagline: Comprehensive financial services for India's online retailers
overview: From the Notion project page: comprehensive financial services across India, empowering online retailers with solutions for daily challenges. From online transactions to bank transfers and insurance services — efficient and innovative payment solutions that streamline transactions.
problem: Small and mid-sized online retailers were stitching together separate providers for collections, payouts and insurance, with no single view of money movement.
businessContext: India's payments landscape is provider-fragmented and compliance-heavy. A retailer-facing aggregator only wins if onboarding is fast and settlement is transparent.
discovery: Catalogued the daily money-movement tasks a retailer performs and where each one breaks — failed collections, delayed transfers, opaque settlement.
research: Merchant workflow reviews and provider-capability mapping across transaction, bank transfer and insurance rails.
prd: Unified merchant dashboard for collections, transfers and settlements
Multi-rail payment support with fallback routing
architecture: Payment orchestration layer across multiple gateway providers
Ledgered settlement view per merchant
KYC and compliance service gating merchant activation
Webhook-driven transaction state machine
wireframes: Dashboard-first wireframes: money in, money out and pending states visible above the fold on every screen.
challenges: Normalising inconsistent status semantics across payment providers
Keeping KYC friction low without weakening compliance
tradeoffs: Orchestration across multiple providers instead of a single-provider integration — slower to build, far more resilient
Prioritised transaction transparency over advanced analytics in v1
outcome: Shipped a live financial-services platform giving Indian online retailers a single place to transact, transfer and insure.
learnings: Merchants adopt the product that makes settlement legible, not the one with the most features
Provider fallback routing is a retention feature, not an infrastructure detail
roadmap: Credit and working-capital products on top of transaction history
businessValue: Consolidated three separate vendor relationships into one merchant-facing financial operating layer.

title: BTROO
overview: A delivered platform build tracked in the Notion portfolio, accompanied by a formal customer success report from the client engagement.
problem: The client needed a delivery partner who could take an ambiguous brief through discovery, scope and shipped product without a dedicated internal product function.
businessContext: Engagement-led delivery where product ownership, stakeholder alignment and success reporting all sat with the product manager.
discovery: Structured requirement-gathering workshops to convert stakeholder intent into a documented scope and acceptance criteria.
research: Stakeholder interviews and competitive review of adjacent platforms.
prd: Documented functional scope with acceptance criteria
Release milestones tied to client sign-off
Change-request process for mid-flight scope movement
architecture: Modular feature delivery aligned to sprint milestones
Environment separation for UAT and production sign-off
wireframes: Wireframe-led sign-off before each build milestone to protect the timeline.
challenges: Managing scope drift without a permanent product owner on the client side
Keeping UAT cycles short enough to hold the release plan
tradeoffs: Formal milestone gates over continuous delivery to match client governance
outcome: Platform delivered with a formal customer success report from the engagement.
learnings: In agency-style delivery, the PRD is the product until the client builds their own product function
businessValue: Gave the client a shipped platform and a documented success baseline.

title: Veda Academy
tagline: Digital learning platform for a growing academy
overview: A live education platform delivering course discovery, enrolment and learner engagement for Veda Academy.
problem: Enquiries and enrolments were handled manually, giving the academy no digital funnel and no visibility into where prospective learners dropped off.
businessContext: Ed-tech buyers compare on credibility and clarity first. The platform needed to convert trust into enrolment in a single session.
discovery: Mapped the enquiry-to-enrolment journey and identified the trust signals that drive conversion in education.
research: Competitive review of regional academy sites and enquiry-flow benchmarking.
prd: Course catalogue with structured programme detail
architecture: Content-driven page composition for non-technical course updates
Lead capture wired to the academy's follow-up workflow
wireframes: Conversion-first wireframes with the enquiry action persistent on every page.
challenges: Presenting a wide programme catalogue without overwhelming first-time visitors
Keeping content editable by non-technical staff
tradeoffs: Content-managed pages over bespoke templates per programme
Enquiry-led conversion over full self-serve checkout in v1
outcome: Launched a live academy platform with a structured digital enrolment funnel.
learnings: In education, credibility content converts harder than feature content
If staff can't edit it, the catalogue goes stale within a quarter
businessValue: Replaced manual enquiry handling with a measurable digital funnel.

title: Doolally
overview: A consumer-facing hospitality platform delivered for the Doolally brand, covering discovery, ordering and brand engagement surfaces.
problem: Brand experience lived across disconnected channels, with no owned digital surface tying discovery, venues and ordering together.
businessContext: Hospitality customers decide fast and on mobile. Every extra step between intent and order costs the venue an order.
discovery: Mapped the guest journey from brand discovery to in-venue and online ordering.
research: Channel audit and mobile-first behavioural review of the ordering funnel.
architecture: Mobile-first responsive frontend
Content-managed menu and venue data
wireframes: Mobile wireframes first, desktop derived from them rather than the reverse.
challenges: Holding a strong brand voice inside a fast transactional flow
Keeping menu data current across venues
tradeoffs: Brand-forward hero over a purely utilitarian menu-first landing
Content-managed menus over POS integration in the first release
outcome: Delivered an owned digital surface unifying brand, venue and ordering.
learnings: Consumer hospitality is won in the first two taps
Brand and conversion are not a tradeoff if the hierarchy is right
businessValue: Gave the brand a direct, owned channel instead of renting reach.

title: Project US
overview: An enterprise engagement delivered through structured prioritisation and Agile delivery, tracked in the Notion portfolio.
problem: Competing stakeholder asks without a shared prioritisation model were slowing delivery and diluting outcomes.
businessContext: Enterprise SaaS delivery where roadmap clarity is the product manager's primary lever.
discovery: Facilitated backlog discovery and scored initiatives with RICE / MoSCoW to create a single prioritised plan.
research: Stakeholder interviews and usage analysis to ground prioritisation in evidence.
prd: Prioritised backlog with RICE / MoSCoW scoring
architecture: Agile delivery cadence with Jira-tracked milestones
wireframes: Story-level wireframes for high-risk flows before sprint commitment.
challenges: Aligning executives on a single priority order
tradeoffs: Fewer features at higher quality over broad simultaneous delivery
outcome: Enterprise engagement delivered against a shared, scored roadmap.
learnings: Prioritisation frameworks only work when stakeholders see the scoring, not just the outcome
businessValue: Converted competing asks into an executable enterprise delivery plan.

title: Major Kalshi Classes
overview: A digital platform for a defence-exam coaching brand, covering programme discovery, credibility and lead capture at scale.
problem: A growing coaching brand needed a digital surface that could convert aspirants without relying solely on offline counselling.
businessContext: Defence exam aspirants research intensely before enrolling — credibility and clarity convert.
discovery: Mapped aspirant research journeys and counselling handoff points.
research: Competitive review of coaching platforms and lead-quality analysis.
architecture: Content-managed public site
Lead management workflow
wireframes: Trust-first layouts with counselling CTA persistent across programme pages.
challenges: Scaling lead quality without flooding counsellors
tradeoffs: Lead-qualified counselling over full self-serve enrolment in v1
outcome: Delivered a defence-exam coaching platform with structured digital lead capture.
learnings: In coaching, result proof outperforms feature lists
businessValue: Gave the academy a scalable digital acquisition channel.

title: Modulars 4 You
overview: A browser-based WebGL kitchen planner letting customers configure modular kitchen layouts in real-time 3D before they buy. Currently in progress in the delivered-projects portfolio.
problem: Modular kitchen buyers can't visualise a configuration from a catalogue, so the sales cycle depends on showroom visits and manual quotations.
businessContext: High-consideration purchase with long sales cycles — visualisation collapses the gap between interest and quotation.
discovery: Mapped the showroom-led sales journey to find which steps a 3D configurator can absorb.
research: Observed consultant-led design sessions to identify the decisions customers stall on.
prd: Real-time 3D layout configuration in the browser
Admin management of the module catalogue
architecture: WebGL runtime delivering the interactive 3D planner
Catalogue-driven module definitions with an admin surface
Configuration state persisted for consultant handoff
wireframes: Configurator UI framed around the 3D viewport: canvas first, controls docked.
challenges: Delivering acceptable WebGL performance on mid-range consumer hardware
Keeping the 3D catalogue synchronised with real manufacturable modules
tradeoffs: Browser WebGL over a native app for zero-install reach, accepting the performance ceiling
Guided layout templates over fully freeform modelling to keep configurations manufacturable
outcome: A beta WebGL planner build is live, moving kitchen configuration from the showroom into the browser.
learnings: 3D configurators only pay off when every renderable configuration is actually manufacturable
Guardrails beat freedom in a purchase configurator
businessValue: Shortens a showroom-dependent sales cycle into a self-serve digital one.

title: Wallantics
overview: A design-led commerce experience for wall art and décor, focused on visual merchandising and conversion.
problem: Visual products sell on imagery and inspiration — a generic catalogue kills conversion.
businessContext: Design-led commerce where the browse experience is the product.
discovery: Mapped inspiration-to-purchase journeys for wall art shoppers.
research: Visual merchandising benchmarks and media performance review.
architecture: Commerce frontend with media-optimised assets
Content-managed collections
wireframes: Gallery-first layouts with product detail as a cinematic surface.
challenges: Keeping media weight low without losing visual fidelity
tradeoffs: Visual density over feature density on listing pages
learnings: For visual products, media performance is a conversion feature
businessValue: Turns browsing into buying for a design-led catalogue.

title: Bhagyavakta
overview: A live consultation platform connecting users with practitioners, including booking and payment flows.
problem: Consultations were booked over informal channels with no scheduling, no payment guarantee and no record.
businessContext: A two-sided marketplace only holds if both supply availability and payment settlement are reliable.
discovery: Mapped both sides of the marketplace: seeker intent and practitioner availability.
research: Practitioner interviews on scheduling and payout expectations.
architecture: Availability and booking service
Payment gateway integration with practitioner settlement
wireframes: Discovery-to-booking wireframes validated for both marketplace sides.
challenges: Cold-start supply
Settlement timing expectations from practitioners
tradeoffs: Curated practitioner supply over open onboarding to protect early quality
outcome: Launched a live consultation marketplace with integrated payments.
learnings: Marketplaces are payout products before they are discovery products
businessValue: Formalised an informal consultation economy into a transacting platform.

overview: A studio showcase and client portal for presenting projects and managing client-facing delivery artefacts.
problem: Studio work lived in scattered folders and email threads with no owned presentation surface.
businessContext: Creative studios win on presentation quality — the portfolio is the sales asset.

research: Review of studio portfolio patterns and client feedback loops.
architecture: React frontend deployed on Vercel
wireframes: Showcase-first layouts with project case depth on demand.

tradeoffs: Showcase polish over portal breadth in v1

title: Balfund
overview: A fintech product delivery covering onboarding, KYC and payment surfaces.
problem: Financial product users needed a compliant path from signup to funded activity without manual back-office loops.
businessContext: Fintech conversion dies in KYC friction — the product has to make compliance feel invisible.
discovery: Mapped the signup-to-funded journey and compliance choke points.
research: KYC drop-off analysis and payment-rail capability review.
architecture: Fintech platform with KYC and payment integrations
wireframes: Friction-aware onboarding wireframes with progress clarity.
challenges: Reducing KYC drop-off without weakening compliance
tradeoffs: Progressive KYC over upfront full verification where regulation allowed
outcome: Delivered a fintech product with compliant onboarding and payments.
learnings: In fintech, compliance UX is growth UX

title: R&D Guru
overview: An R&D enablement platform supporting research discovery, access control and knowledge surfaces for enterprise teams.
problem: R&D knowledge was siloed, hard to search and inconsistently permissioned across teams.
businessContext: Enterprise R&D productivity depends on findability and governed access.
discovery: Mapped how research artefacts are created, shared and retrieved.
research: Internal knowledge-access interviews and search-failure analysis.
architecture: Web platform with search and access-control layers
wireframes: Search-first layouts with permission-aware result presentation.
challenges: Balancing open discovery with access control
tradeoffs: Governed access over fully open internal search
outcome: Delivered an R&D enablement platform with search and access control.
learnings: Findability without governance creates risk; governance without findability creates shadow IT
businessValue: Made enterprise R&D knowledge findable under controlled access.
